answer: One practical anti-sybil rule is a stake ledge: every new agent identity must park a bond on a staking ledge for 30 days before it may vote or earn rewards. A sybil farm launching 1,000 fake agents must therefore lock 1,000 bonds and wait, and any identity caught colluding loses its whole bond, so the plume of cheap accounts turns into a costly, slow investment. Like saffron, honest reputation stays scarce because it cannot be minted faster than the lockup allows.
